correctness.rationale: The mathematical condition is exactly a clique condition in a finite graph. Each output ball is built with exact deletion and at-most-one flip and crosschecked by an independently written string procedure for all 480 nontrivial inputs. At lengths five through eight the checked cliques have sizes 18, 26, 26, 24. The self-contained exhaustive search properly colors all residual candidate graphs, explores every unpruned clique branch, and completes with no larger clique. Its source is CHECKER.cpp, and OUTPUT.txt records successful replay and precise search-node totals. At lengths one through four all output intersections are below nine by the total output-domain size. No infinite extrapolation is made.

value.rationale: The nine-read threshold is explicitly motivated by a recent mixed-error reconstruction construction. Its exact initial finite capacities are operationally relevant upper bounds under the formal code definition. The first strict decline as source length grows, from 26 to 24, exposes a natural nonmonotonic boundary missed by asymptotic redundancy constructions. This is not a routine one-length increment of an existing nine-read finite table; the entire initial profile through the first decline is determined with explicit witnesses and a complete upper-bound computation.
